newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends $2.75 firmer on US products rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends $2.75 firmer on US products rally.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures last traded up $2.75 a tonne on Thursday on the back of late strength in U.S. products, traders said.

The front-month March contract finished at $164.75, 25 cents off the session high, after a rally of $2 a tonne in the last hour of business. It had traded around $162 to $163 for much of the afternoon.

IPE April Brent was trading at $19.50 a barrel at 1743 GMT, up 10 cents on the day but seven cents off the high. The prompt intermonth April/May Brent spread moved out to +30 cents from +24 cents in midday.
"We just got on the back of gasoline strength in the U.S. and were carried up by that rally," a trader said.
Traders in New York said gasoline-to-crude crack spreads were firming on short covering and even buying. Gasoline on NYMEX was trading up 0.67 cent at 64 cents a gallon.
A combination of poor physical demand, news of increased OPEC production and crude run cuts by a handful of European refineries were fuelling the bearish tone.
"There's really nothing out there in terms of fundamentals to help the market higher," said a broker.
Crude oil production by OPEC rose 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.77 million bpd in February, according to a Reuters survey.
The increase comes on top of extra non-OPEC volumes and at a time when European refineries are heading for spring maintenance programmes, which cuts demand for crude.
Some dealers, however, took a crumb of comfort from a modest improvement in the Brent/gas oil crack spread, which moved out to $2.78 a barrel from $2.31 on Wednesday.
